reviews.review_description: Good sales and service. Slow for parts to arrive over summer 2019, then install went ok but couldn't connect due to meter issues. Then covid delays and elec upgrade took ages. 18 months from signing up to turning the system on.
Good service and hope panels and inverter can stay the period proposed for the money spend

Although initially quite pleased with the process of getting our solar from Energy Aware, we have found them to be lacking when we had fire caused by a faulty DC isolator on our roof, they called it a installation fault and our installation warranty had finished 5 months previous.Initially when speaking to them I was told that we would be looked after as our warranty was not long ended.... famous last words, we managed to get the repairs covered by insurance and asked Energy Aware to cover the $500 excess, they then pulled “I have spoken to the manager and he said that it was not covered by warranty, so we will not be paying anything”.DC isolator was supposed to be weather proof, I was told that the fire caused by a faulty DC isolator which they supplied, be careful when dealing with Energy Aware... profits are number one, not my family’s safety, if this was my company I would be very concerned with this happening with systems that I had installed.
Sales and quote was good, the salesperson was helpful and conscientious. The system is yet to be installed so I cannot make further comments.

Clear and good advice along the wayThe installation was well organised and ran like clockwork which was great since I was working from home. The installer consulted with us through out the work which made us really comfortableWe are connected to the grind and fascinated to be able to watch our panels produce electricity over the day

Quick and happy to answer any questionsInstallation went off without an problems the arrived on time and the workers were polite and explained everything clearlyGrid connection and organised by the company we only has to be here as the inverter is inside out garage we have has no problems.  The app on the phone is great and easy to read.

This was a terrible experiance, after getting over 10 different quotes I decided to use energy aware as they had given me dates and agreed to the specifications that I had requested.We HAD to sign up that day to get the deal and to get it in the time frame we wanted it in.Application with Tas Networks would be submitted as soon as the deposit was made. [which proved to be very incorrect]2 points were made very clear,Completely Black Frames as the panels were on the front face of the house.A Smart meter was to be installed.Timeframe was VERY drawn out.The second lot of panels werenâ€™t much better than the first, and a lower grade panel, to which I really think you should have given us a discount or the extra panels.A Hybrid Fronius Symo inverter would be installed so I could add Batteries down the track.

After 8 months of emails and phone calls to replace our inverter, under warranty, we are still waiting. They are happy to take your money but when there is a problem they just keep passing the buck. We would not recommend Energy Aware to anyone
Price includes a battery as the system is for a farm stock watering project where water is required 24 hours

Out of the three companies you put me onto only one got back with a serious quote which was energy aware. One said they would send through a quote but couldn't get onto the job and the other told me up front they were expensive and would send a quote but nothing ever came of it. Energy aware are great to deal with. They have kept me informed through the whole process and haven't installed yet due to rainy weather. I wouldn't get up there either in the wet so I'm happy to wait till the right time for them. Thank you for your help with solar and I found your web page very informative. Cheers Mandi

We bought Trinia panels with SMA inverter. System generates about 28kw a day in summer and 22-24 in winter, so happy with that. Products are great, its the service which is poor. After a storm, cable ties that had broken washed down the downpipe from the roof and caught on the leaf guard. A spanner would appear on the SMA screen saying check insulation and power generator. Sent a photo of the screen to Energy Aware asking for advice....still nothing. Their customer service is poor

Energy Aware did not come to the house to quote.  Quoted on 20 panels.  When the installers came they could only fit 19.They then saidWe have just received word from ###### on site that he is encountering significant difficulties with the tile situation on your roof and this is blowing out install times significantly. There is also an issue with your board and we will need to swap out your main switch. Additional costs come to:Main Switch: $150Roof work: $450They had rung my wife saying the same thing even before the installers had arrived (they later said they were confused with the morning job).  Is this a pattern?The main switch was not changed and the roof has been there for 65 years, so was no different to the time of the quotation.This claim was ultimately dropped.The installers came 3 hours late and did not finish.  The job was therefore delayed for 3 weeks (christmas)  When they came it took the team 6 hours to finish the job so there was no way they could have completed the job in an afternoon on the original visit.
Will know more when we have it installed late may feel free to get back to us

Energy Aware gave great information, were timely, and communicative. The other two you suggested were not as thorough and gave us conflicting information. We don't have an installation date yet, but they said it will be in about 2 to 3 weeks. Thanks for all your help. Much appreciated.

The company I dealt with didn't quite deliver what they promised, however the sub contracted installer was excellent.  The company rang me and advised me the supplier would be there at 8am, and at 9am, I rang them back, to be told that they were having trouble with a forklift and were running a bit late.  Installer arrived at 9.10, and advised me that they don't start work until 9am, so never should have been booked in for 8am.  Salesman then rang me about 30 minutes after installer arrived, and told me he had just spoken to the installer and they would be there in 10 minutes. I then stopped him and advised him that they were already there, and that I had now been lied to by 3 different staff members.  Installer 5 stars, Salesman and office staff 0 stars

Our experience at quoting and installation stages was excellent.   Installed September 2013 we've had good as expected returns.October 2018 and our Aurora invertor stops working and displays an error code E031. Call Energy Aware who state "Oh what a shame its one month out of warranty " Around $2000 to replace after only 5 years!!  We are in the process of collating our AGL bills to show the invertor stopped working within the warranty period. Lets see how we go??

Matthew from Energy Aware & the installation team were all courteous, professional & respectful.   The installation was done 2 days ago & no mess was left behind.   The Trina Honey panels were installed with a Zeversolar inverter Zeverlution 5000.   It's early days but with some reasonable sun today I was able to connect wirelessly & noted attainment of over 22 kWh by 3:40pm.    My daily average over the past 2 months was 20.77 kWh so it is looking promising to achieve payback & benefits from the system.
Good value for money. Quality panels and inverter, easy installation done in a timely manner

Good communication and information. Helpful.Friendly, competent, efficient installers.Region - Northern Spencer Gulf. Roof facing due North.System seems very sensitive and has an output of up to 2.5Kw on August -September days (its maximum is 3.2Kw). Very pleased with this. The new import/export meter hasn't been installed yet and so I can see the current analogue meter going backwards - profit, profit, profit.Summer cooling is via a ducted evaporative system.As a small power user overall in a traditional three bedroom house I have calculated that I will pay off my investment in under five years, perhaps even sooner, helped by the AGL feed-in tariff.

We were late in accepting the quote (by about 8 months) but Energy Aware still honoured the original quote. It took 4 months for them to install the system due to the Christmas break, electrician on holidays etc and a heavy workload, but 3 men arrived one day and it was all installed and up and running by 2.30 that afternoon. Neat job. No complaints.Energy Aware have provided lots of information about the system and are tracking the installation of our new meter box which is the responsibility of the area energy company.

At the start Energy Aware were very helpful and consistently called to find out where we were at with our decision on solar but as soon as the deposit was paid all contact was stopped.  After 2 weeks I had to start calling to find out why they had not emailed the deposit receipt and to find out what was happening with our installation. Still waiting to hear when installation will start and I am really starting to have second thoughts about going with Energy Aware.
We have ordered system and waiting on installation
There are many variables which impact on the decision ie. panel location, warranty periods, manufacturing origin / reliability, its not just about price. Over Christmas there was limited service
System should be installed in a week or 2. 10 kw system. Essential energy limiting me to 5 kw export !!!! Unexpected !
Installer. Jeremy, did a professional job. All was neat and tidy and exactly as I wanted it.No rubbish or tools left behind.
It was a great experience, System so far looks good. just waiting to have it connected to the grid. Great company to deal with. Thanks for all your help and advice.
Not yet installed
After asking for a quote, Energy Aware's presentation, paperwork and process was very accurate and easy to understand.Their installers were professional, approachable and completed a tidy job.

I had a wide range of experiences. I actually went for 5 quotes...only 2 from those recommended by Solarquotes. I was given a wide range of information - some a bit confusing and conflicting of others, and a wide range of prices. Every one of them told me they had the absolute best panels and inverters and most of them were different brands. Do your research.  I went for a good quality system and got a reasonable price I feel. To be installed in the next week or so, so time will tell.
Only received the one quote via your website , found 2 others myself but went with Energy Aware

Until now I would have rated the whole system as fantastic, but now that the Clenergy inverter has failed after only 6 years I can only rate it overall as good.  The rest of the system and service is fantastic, the inverter is poor.  I believe EnergyAware now use SMA and Zeversolar inverters.  I see that SMA are excellent and believe the Zeversolar are Chinese made but owned by SMA, so hopefully better than Clenergy.  I will report back on my replacement inverter once I have some history.
Peter in the NT organised everything for us including Gov rebate and connection to grid. All done within a few weeks.

What people need to be mindful of is not what they want by what their wholesaler will allow.  We sought a 5.78 kVA jinko panels x 275 KVA system with a hybrid (solaX) inverter in which to add batteries to the system when affordable but our Wholesaler "Ausnet" rejected the application by the supplier with Ausnet indicating that they needed to protect their poles and wires and that the other .78 KVA could effect the integrity of their system/supply and therefore made a policy to only allow <5 KVA systems . Ausnet are a monopoly in Victoria in which I obtained no satisfaction.
They installed the panels and INnverter last Friday and I haven't had it connected to the grid yet.

We installed an extra solar system and new smart inverter. The installation process was poor due to poor planning and they miscalculated how many panels would fit - underestimated. This was significant for us as we needed to maximise solar for going off grid.

Hi Fin : Have at this stage only paid the deposit. No instillation has been done yet. Will let you know when installed. I told Nick Burrows from Energy Aware that l always go for quality and he assures me that there systems and workmanship are.Thanks Glynn Sutton

At time of writing, have 10 of 18 panels installed, 3 weeks after initial installation.This due to roof supports being further apart than is standard.(so the installers needed twice as many panel support brackets as planned - and didn't have spares)I have been charged extra for these additional brackets ($400) and have to presume that this is a reasonable price.Energy Aware has already offered 1 date to complete the installation which I was unable to accept for various reasons, so Energy Aware have been quite proactive in trying to achieve completion.
Stuck to time scaleInstalled within 3 weeks
I will try to remember to send further comments when the system has been installed.
Quite a while between accepting quote and installation.
Josh from Energy Aware had terrific follow up and answered all my questions very ably.  He was honest about a necessary additional cost ( two story) requiring special equipment

Energy Aware were keen to do business but not in an over the top sales manner. They provided a timely quotation and when I realised that the size had to change they were obliging and re-quoted promptly with an alteration to suit my specific request. The installer contacted me to arrange a suitable date and arrived on the agreed time. He worked without break all day with a high standard of finish on his work. The installer also took time to explain the operation of the system.

Deposit paid 21st April, job completed 21st July, Energy Aware was not aware of what was needed by SA Power Networks in regard to asbestos being on board. electrician did not turn up on final install day and the solar network had to return and install the new meter board themselves. Ensure the solar company either works in the state you live, or understands what is required by each state body.

I was sceptical when they quoted and took my deposit without doing a site inspection. I had to chase them up a month after I paid the deposit  to find out what was going on with the installation as I had not heard back from them. They installed on the day they said they would , the quality of the workmanship looks good and the system is exactly what was quoted. The installers were courteous , professional and cleaned up most of their mess.
Still awaiting Tas Networks to perform infrastructure upgrades before the system can be turned on, but the system has been tested and works.

My system is up and running - so happy to be solar again! These newer systems seem to be much more efficient than the first array I installed on my last house about ten years ago. The inverter is a neat, unobtrusive unit and it even has a wifi connection to my computer. Now, please make this rain go away and the sun shine in Tasmania! ;-)

Our 40 degree pitched Cathedral Ceiling two storey home was a challenging installation project, and before we committed to purchasing this system, Energy Aware were happy to have one of their accredited electricians, Steve Mance, inspect our situation and work out how best to do the job and lay out the panels and cabling etc.  The difficulty of roof access made it necessary to use a boom lift for the two days required to install the panels and supporting rails, and this added to the cost, but as everything was clearly explained, we were happy to proceed.  The system is performing better than we expected given the orientation was to the North East with up to 4.5 kW being generated late morning and up to 32kW on a clear day, so we are very happy customers!
As yet my system is not installed
Great contact sales personcompetetive quote within dollars of the rest but affable and diligent salespersonlocal installer and close to the site offering backup and support

I put the system in 3 years ago and was very pleased and impressed with Energy Aware's service. Whilst most of their input was administrative, the various sub-contractors they assembled were well coordinated, turned up on time and did a great job. The higher than normal cost of installation for a 5kW system was because we chose to install on a shed roof remote from the main house, which necessitated running underground cables. Again EA's contractors did a good job.I'm posting now because just before Christmas our inverter (Aurora) died and I want to commend Energy Aware for their fantastic service. Despite it being the holiday period, they got the ball rolling quickly, efficiently and without any dispute and had their local contractor install the replacement immediately it arrived. A shame to lose 3 weeks output at such a sunny time of year, but, when I read of other peoples problems getting warranty issues settled, I am well pleased with the super efficient response of Julian and his team. Thanks
I havent yet had it installed but have had a great service so far and the team have been very helpful with information.
Very pleased to be able to use your service to obtain quotes and chat to reps of all three companies. Thank you for setting up this site.
Cannot say a lot at present as nothing has been done as yet.
Had a long wait for SA Power Networks to reprogramme the meter

The supplier acted quickly, and communication was great.  Due to bad weather, my installation took a little longer to wait for. The installers turned up on the day, and did a good job, took less than a day, and was working well when they finished
Great guys to deal with , very understanding as I was offshore trying to organise this with limited phone reception , very pleased with the support .
Local tradespeople, accessible contacts and value for money products. I would not have found these people without Solar Quotes website.
Although inverter failed within 10 days of installation, Energy Aware and installing electrician very responsive and replaced within a couple of days.

The one thing that impressed me with the people at the other end of the phone is that they were courteous, polite and knew their business. They followed up what they said they would and have been helpful with questions we had asked. On top of that, I did not feel pressured nor did they try and up sell me even when I was in doubt of a bigger system or not. I have not yet had the system installed, but I would say that they would be above par with most tradesmen I have worked with over the years.
Installer's communication was quite vague.System was damaged by high winds within a few weeks and had to be repaired by the installer, communications still vague.

All suppliers did'nt offer too much info - I needed to know what questions to ask. Ended up with 3.5kW system. Due to the positioning of my house (narrow north exposure) my installation possibly could have been designed better.
I really don't know anything about the system that is on my roof.

Easy to get overwhelmed with the amount of information available on the web. I was able to speak to the salesperson who gave me quite a bit of time, stepping me through the entire process and answered all my questions. The installation team also need a mention here; my house is old and running the wires was quite difficult but they did a great job.

I signed up Energy Aware in August 2013 with installation finally going ahead 4 months later.  Installation was undertaken by sub-contractor Lifestyle Electrical, they were very efficient and did a good job as they were subjected to varying weather conditions (ie wind and rain) during the day.Following the installation I decided to set up a PC and install Growatt's inverter monitoring software, this is where I found out that I had not received the 5.0 kW inverter I had ordered, while the label indicated it was a 5kW inverter, it would only produce 4.6 kW, while my location might only permit maximum generation one (1) day in a year in optimum conditions, I wanted what I had ordered.After much toing and froing via email and telephone discussions with Energy Aware followed by discussions with other people in the solar industry I established that an inverter firmware upgrade or modification would allow the inverter to generate 5kW.  I obtained and successfully installed the software modifying the inverter which now will produce 5kW.  The whole process has taken me approx 8 months to resolve. I have had to undertake a lot of research (I feel Energy Aware could have done more to find a resolution and not leave it up to me) into what could be done. If Energy Aware had replaced the inverter I would have lost Aurora's higher feed-in tariff, but Aurora advises that a firmware update/modification do not have any affect and do not need to know anything about it.My experience evokes the obvious question, how many other people have ordered a system, had it installed and are not aware that they did not get what they ordered?  If I had not shown an interest in what was being generated and installed Growatt's monitoring software onto a PC, I too may have been left totally unaware that I had been supplied with a product that I had not ordered.
Impressed with the customer service. Graham Patten was very helpful even after we have confirmed our order. Gives prompt replies.
The guys that did the install were professional, I am very happy with the way it all went.

I found  the company Energy Aware(John Dicmanis) excellent with his patience and information; as with all the people I spoke to in relation to the transaction/installation.I rang on the Tuesday to find out "when" and they arranged the installation on the Friday (the power out in my district on Thurs, otherwise it would have happened sooner.)The 2 lads (from SA Home Electrical - the installers)  were very polite/well dressed in uniform /efficient, & with clean van etc.I would reccommend them.                         So far, so good.

The problem with writing a review of PV installation is that the actual work is so frequently subbed out to electrical contractors. In my case the installation work was done, very capably, by Lifestyle Electrical in Hobart, on behalf of Energy Aware. Lifestyle we would definitely use again. Energy Aware? Not so much! They botched the original site design because they refused to visit for an actual site inspection, relying solely on Google Maps to estimate the number and location of panels. As a consequence, their plan for 20 panels needed to be scaled down to 17. They tried to sell us a two-inverter solution when only a single inverter was ultimately required. And they botched the paperwork to the electricity utility, resulting in weeks of delays and the possibility that our application might have been ruled ineligible for the more generous legacy tariff. Thankfully, we had insisted on a penalty provision whereby they had to reduce the bill by $200 for each week they were late -- otherwise we might still be waiting as some other customers are.

The waiting is awful. No one came out to inspect the property, I had too email all details , picture of meter box,where it is -what side of the house its on, measure my own roof , tell them which way my roof was facing. 6 weeks later my meter got reset , now I have to wait for the install of the system.

Very professional sales people - kept me up to date with changes in legislation etc.  Did not do a hard sell, but called to follow me up etc.Installers were really good - on time, professional, neat.The actual install was really well done.  Work safe came and did an inspection and made the comment that the installation company is one of the better ones.
Not installed yet. Declined house roof install as shading of dormer windows limited output. Devonport Electrical will install online meter

I was a bit disappointed that Energy Aware assessed my property with google earth and under estimated the size of the roof. A third of the system had to be mounted on the east facing roof. There were a few delays with supply and installation but their customer service was very helpful and dealt with each problem with professional courtesy.
I embarked on this project from a cold call which, I signed up with and then backed out of within the cooling off period. I wish I had known about your service before I dived in.
Like to use a local company and installers were very good, done a top job.
There were some delays with installation, but they took $100 off the price to compensate for lost savings on my power bill.Overall, I found Energy Aware were a good company to deal with.
The system has been operating now for 1 year & 9 months. No complaints.

Had my solar system installed about a year and a half ago. The installation was very poor. The inverter is not what I was told. Panels fell over. They repaired that problem but when I approached them about other problems, it fell on deaf ears. I have been waiting for a reply now for many months

Energy Aware were great to deal with.I was able to negotiate a great price and install was neat and tidy.The system was up and running within two weeks. Cannot fault this company.Thank you Energy Aware.

We took advice from Finn on the quality of panels and decided to upgrade to the best quality available, i.e. REC panels combined with a SMA  Sunnyboy inverter, to be installed by Energy Aware.Our roof is facing NW. The roof pitch is only 6 degrees, so we have ordered tilt frames to maximise the angle for light. We already have a 1.1 kilowatt system installed that operates at about 80 percent efficiency due to some shading from trees.When our new system is installed we will have 6.1 kilowatts in total. Our water is heated by a solar tube system that combines brilliantly with a timer for electric boost in winter between 6am and 8am and 6pm and 8 pm. Our aim is to eliminate hydro bills totally as we are about to become pensioners and will likely not be able to afford power bills as they continue to rise every year.

I would like to say your website was most informative on helping me decide what kind of system to get. I was able to do my own research based on your information to make a well informed decision on what make of panels and inverter to get. Thanks very much for your valued information.Energy Aware seems to be backlogged and has not installed my system yet. It's been well over a month now but I was assured the installation will be soon.

We decided to accept the quote from Energy Aware.  It was very detailed and explained exactly what we got and how much to expect in savings a year on our electricity, the exact costs and the difference between paying up front and using a payment method.  They take a deposit and allow you to make repayments until the system is paid off which is handy for us as we did not have all the money upfront.  The fortnightly repayments are $70 and we worked out we save more than that saving electricity and using the solar instead so it really pays for itself and a bit more.The solar installers contacted me shortly after and made a day and time to install which was only a week away from the call.  So, it was very quickly installed although it took the work men all day to complete it from 8.30 am to 5 pm, they did a great job.  No Mess was left behind and they explained how it worked and how to read the box information.Aurora, the electricity company, came after 3 days and completed the link up and so now we are receiving solar power which is fantastic.The Company kept us up to date regarding the installation and emailed through all relevant information and repayment details. Very helpful and professional.I recommend Energy Aware very highly.

Energy Aware were very prompt with a quote and sending paperwork etc., but once the deposit was paid and the contract signed I found they were quite slow and getting everything else sorted.I sent a number of emails because I had not heard from them and they did reply within 2 working days.  My contract was signed on 7th June but still not installed.  Installation due on 7th August.  If I was as slow at repaying as they have been at arranging install I am sure they would not be happy.
Install still isn't done, waiting 6 weeks so far. Hopefully, sooner the better.
Offered 2 grades of equipment which I appreciated.Matched other cheaper quotes.Installer Roy Martin PGS Solar based in Devonport impressed me with his knowledge and exceptionally tidy installation.

Energy aware were very professional and helpful. They kept me informed at all times  during the process.The installers PSG electrical were excellent they did a great job even down to the way they arranged the solar panels on the roof to fit in with the existing panels from a previous install.
Well, they were all good people but in the end we gave it to energy aware for a good price, but not much on people skills they didn't keep us in the loop.

Received full documentation of the system I wanted. Helpful notes as to procedures for installation. Queries answered promptly and fully. Kept informed as to status of date of installation. Delayed by a few days from original date due to a prior problem install but these things happen. Installation carried out professionally and given comprehensive instructions on use. A very good experience in all.
I have put good in the quality section but as it is not fully installed I can not say if is good or bad yet.

It took almost 3 weeks from the time of installation of the panels for the company to submit the Electrical Works Request to the power company so they could come and do the meter work and activate the system. This cost me quite a lot in lost energy production.The Energy Aware representative repeatedly lied to me about the EWR, telling me it had been submitted. I finally contacted Aurora Energy myself. This seemed to light a fire under Energy Aware. The EWR was submitted almost immediately and the connections were made within 10 days.All in all, it took almost a month from the time the panels were installed for the work to be completed and the system activated. The electrical contractor did excellent work and was very professional. I would recommend them with no hesitation. It's Energy Aware that I have a problem with.

It took almost 3 weeks from the time of installation of the panels for the company to submit the Electrical Works Request to the power company so they could come and do the meter work and activate the system. This cost me quite a lot in lost energy production. The Energy Aware representative repeatedly lied to me about the EWR, telling me it had been submitted. I finally contacted Aurora Energy myself. This seemed to light a fire under Energy Aware. The EWR was submitted almost immediately and the connections were made within 10 days. All in all, it took almost a month from the time the panels were installed for the work to be completed and the system activated. The electrical contractor did excellent work and was very professional. I would recommend them with no hesitation. It's Energy Aware that I have a problem with.
There was a couple holdups with the install but all in all we are happy with what we got.
We had quite a good experience with the installation, quality tradesman and service.We would recommend using this website to obtain quotes and make your choice.
Office staff were not very helpful, but otherwise  the service is good.

Of the 3 suppliers you suggested, North Group, Jim's Solar & Energy Aware, the latter went out of their way to answer all my queries.My only concern with them was the length of time they've been in business as I want my supplier to be around in the future to service any warranty claims. I paid my deposit today so the installation will be in a few week's time. I am ticking "no" to using my review simply because it hasn't been installed yet.However, if you contact me after the installation is complete, I would be more than happy to submit a review.I must confess that I would not consider "Jim's Solar" because we have "Jim's Mowing", "Jim's Pest Control" & possibly other franchises owned by "Jim". I don't think "Jim" can have expertise in all these fields, especially solar!

The supplier has been good however the installer or sub-contractor for Energy Aware keeps promising a date to install the system and then doesn't turn up. We are disappointed about this aspect of the installation.
Pleased. I only had to pay small deposit before installation.
Consultant (Daniel) was excellent and answered all my questions in a professional and timely manner. Provided information that was relevant and seemed to provide honest feedback.

We had some problems relating to size and positioning but these were resolved quickly. The installation was done with minimum fuss and disruption. The electrician likewise did his job very efficiently.

On the ball, very professional, within the time frame given. Arrived when stated and cleaned up afterwards. Excellent tradesmen, especially the Electrician, Nelson South, who was most pedantic about the whole installation. They worked for 11 hours in POURING RAIN to get the installation done and we never heard one word of complaint nor a suggestion that they come back another day. The Salesman explained and sent all the relevant information via email so we could study and understand how solar works, and was available to answer any questions we had.  It is now very nice to check and see we are using 19 kW and at the same time 190 kW are going into the grid.

Dealings with Energy Aware were very good. The installers were not so good. They were late for their appointed arrival time by 7 hours and did not finish on the day as agreed. There was rubbish left that had to be cleaned up. The installation itself was good. The time between the solar panel installation and the new meter installation was disappointing.

The installer and his team were excellent and he was something of a perfectionist. The job had a few awkward aspects due to the roof height and slope, wind and some difficulties in running cable in the wall. This meant that it took 1.5 days - longer than was planned and I suspect the installer would not have made any profit. I provided detailed information to Energy Aware, including photos and a roof plan, but they should have done a site visit when quoting. I found Energy Aware excellent to deal with as they took account of my requirements and provided good information. This was not the case with another supplier I considered (not recommended by Solar Quotes). The 2 kW system has been working very well since the meter was installed last week, yielding over 13 kWh on sunny days.

Their salesman John was excellent, helpful, honest, communicative, I know its been a busy time, system not yet installed,(was promised before end of last year).  Communication about installation has been awful, in fact none, John is trying to find out about an install date for me. Hopefully it will be soon.

Installation was quick and efficient but I still can't use my solar panels because I am waiting on confirmation from Essential Energy for Grid connection this was done 16/11/12, pity they weren't as efficient as Energy Aware.Installer explained unit thoroughly and was not surprised that he couldn't finish the job or organize electrician for completion.
Efficient installation. Neat and tidy. Performed work when they said they would. Hassle free.

Great communication from quote thru to final payment. Sensible price negotiation without BS. Friend paid twice what I did based on German designed equipment - but it was ALL still made in China. Jeremy the installer was great. Very clean and efficient installation with full explanation at the end.AGL not very helpful talking to call centre overseas but when I finally got on to an Aussie  I got all the answers about change from existing contract to new tariffs etc. Suggest all buyers should get info from their energy supplier before signing any contract for PV installation. If you are not happy with what you hear then threaten to take your business elsewhere. The supplier might say you are under contract so you can't go elsewhere but they might also say that since you have installed solar you have voided the contract so they will increase your tariff - they can try to play it both ways to suit themselves.Our roof faces NNE and has huge poplars on the eastern neighboring property & roof pitch is not ideal at around 15/20 degrees so we don't get to "full power" on a sunny day till after 10am at about 2800W. I have washing machine on timer to start after 10am while i am at work. Vacuuming, ironing and dishwasher are done during the day where possible (at weekends if needed). All other non-essential stand-by equipment is turned off at the power point.In the first week we have exported 86 kWh and used 34 kWh from the grid. Before solar panels we were using minimum 63 kWh per week up to 130 kWh during winter.
Energy Aware did everything from install to all the paperwork for connecting to the grid. I call it excellent service.
Sales team and installation were great, little slow between placing order and arranging installation (approx 5 weeeks). Overall company and service was excellent.
Failure of the supplier to make me fully aware of the process of grid connection prior to installation, very untidy, and very confusing.

This is not the fault of Energy Aware, but rather a problem with the industry.Our system was installed on time; however the huge volume of paperwork that needs to be completed by the installation company and your energy supplier, in order for the system to be switched on and allow for feedback back into the grid, meant that we had the panels on our roof doing nothing for 7 weeks. Compliance certificates, new meters to be installed, signing of new contracts with our energy supplier, just held the whole process up, unnecessarily in my view.There must be a more expedient way to do all this, prior to installation.

This company listened when we explained that we had secured funding for this project and wanted a five kW system with max panels to generate maximum amount of power. Other companies quoted low in the hope of securing the work but opted to quote 5kw inverter but panels adequate to generate only 3 or 3.5 kw of power, this was not what we asked for.

Energy Aware has been very easy to deal with, any questions related to the system has been answered promptly and I can ring or email and obtain an answer straight away. The system has yet to be installed but is booked in for the start of June.

Excellent communication, system size and components customised (2.66 kW + Aurora Inverter), because of delivery delays we had solar panels upgraded at no cost and system installed two weeks earlier that expected.Most satisfied.

The people I dealt with at Energy Aware were very friendly and helpful.The crew (all electricians) who installed the system were very efficient,friendly and helpful.I must add the process from start to finish is not a quick one,installation,independant safety inspection and changing of meter(if you have old style of meter) a bit frustrating but you get there in the end.Have not had a bill since new meter was installed so cannot comment on savings

Very good customer service and after sales service.Contract to install was signed on the 15th July and because of personal holiday arrangements requested installation be deferred until at least early August. Full installation completed on 12th August. Independant electrical inspection completed on the 15th August confirming all wiring and safety standards were met.
reviews.inverter_brand: Shenzhen Jingfu Yuan Tech Co Ltd (Other)

reviews.review_description: Initially I sought a quotation from AGL, who is my current electricity retailer, but they were very inflexible, wanting to sell me only their special offer 1.5KW system, even though I made it clear that I wanted a larger system.  They did send a person from their installer Bovis Lend Lease to inspect my site, and he was very thorough and knowledgeable.  I explained to him that I wanted a larger system, and he said that I would be quoted a 3 KW system, but when the quote arrived it was still for the 1.5KW system on special.  So I started to look elsewhere.A very unsatisfactory aspect of planning one of these systems is that it seems impossible to find out from the current electricity supplier what my current usage pattern is hour by hour, although I have had a smart meter installed for over a year and the distributor has told me they manage it remotely.  The retailer must have very detailed information about my usage pattern over the last year, but I can't get it out of them.  It seems to me that to make a really informed decision, given the complex web of PFIT, TOU tariffs, various RECS and other subsidies, you need to know detailed information about your current usage, not just daily, but hour by hour.  It seems to me the retailer and/or distributor should be obliged to make this information freely available to you, preferably in electronic form so you can use Excel etc. to analyse it.  Until that happens, I will not be convinced the government is serious about increasing the residential solar generation pool.
Have been easy to contact when questions need to be asked. They have rung to inform us of progress throughout.

Energy Aware were very good and provided all the answers to the relevant questions and all of the technical data on the product. After all my research I provided them with the model of inverter I deemed to be the best and likewise with the panels.They provided good customer service and good follow-up. The installation was completed on the day scheduled. I am still waiting for the final process with the energy provider, but all in all I am very happy with the service, the system and the process.Thank you also to Finn, for your feedback and support.

I had 3-4 companies call up however these guys explained everything well. They also gave me info on the products they would use and installed the system when they said it would go in.Pretty happy i decided to get it organised.

I shopped around with four different companies. Energy Aware offered me an Italian made inverter and a 250W panel (exactly what I was after) for just over $10,000. This was about $1,500 cheaper than any of my other quotes.The installer (Jeremy) was extremely good and courteous to my needs.Job well done.

I originally signed up with a company that I saw on the TV. After waiting for 3 months for them to install the system I got fed up and asked for my deposit back.I then spoke to 3 different companies and Energy Aware's service and price was the most competitive.The installers did a great job and managed to install the inverter inside my garage after two other companies told me it wasnÃ¢â‚¬â„¢t possible. Very happy!!

The real reason I went for Energy Aware was simple: they were the only company that called promptly and most importantly had a plan ready, tailored for my roof. I.e John D had actually looked at what would fit on my roof, how to orient it and had a price. One other didn't call / follow-up at all, and the other company called about 3 weeks after I had signed a contract with Energy Aware!

Energy Aware came up with the best price but struggled with customer service..From the first phone call and emails these guys were really "on the ball". Excellent communication and negotiated a great price..  But once contract signed that changed.Follow up emails and return phone calls "dried up :-)".Disappointing.Energy Aware are brokers that deliver a great price and that's it.They sub contract the installation work out.Our installation was done by R&R solar installations. Richard and his son were fantastic.Work was carried out in a professional manner. Neat and tidy. Highly recommend.
Installed for over a year now and recieved $1800.00 from Origin last statement. Very nice thank you.

we signed for installation in 3-4 weeks in February (still not installed). THEY HAVE NOT CONTACTED US AT ALL IN THIS TIME (19th April). I have instigated 2 contacts - 1. mid March was told another 3-4 weeks. 2. I phnd this Monday and was told he would check on an installation date and would phone me straight back - 4 hours later I hadn't heard a thing so emailed and got a phone call straight back (NO APOLOGY) "installer might phone me back this week"  Company is energyaware. I am gettting annoyed and nervous about the viability of this company!!!!!! I think I got their name from your site.
I wouldn't hesitate to suggest using Energy Aware to anyone. In fact a friend has used them and has had the same great service as us.

We have had it installed today so don't know to much about the savings yet.We also paid less than $2000.00 after Gov RebateEnergy aware also give discount back to their customers instead of advertising.Our Unit was a 1.9kw

Energy Aware was extremely helpful in all aspects of of the preparation and installation of the solar panels . I could not have been happier with the service . Most of it was done over the internet but there were a couple of phone calls . Any queries I had were answered promptly . Their installer , SA Home Electrical , was equally as professional and did an excellent job . I would be happy to recommend both Energy Aware and SA Home Electrical to anyone wanting solar power .
We found the company and the representatives and installers very professional and helpful at all times. We would recommend the company to anyone who is interested in installing solar panels.

My actual rating would have been 4.5 - 4.75 for all categories i.e. Very Good to Excellent.Energy Aware (Julian) and their subcontractor electricians were able to meet a ridiculously tight deadline (to meet the 30 Sept. tariff change) and to accomodate our whim at altering the system size ( to 2.3kW) at the last minute. Julian was easy to deal with and the installers did a very nice job - making a few subtle changes that I requested on the day.I would advise any prospective customers to remain home on the day so that any installation changes can be dealt with then.Overall we were extremely happy with the job.

Apart from the initial sealing of the deal, follow up service has been hit and miss.  Unfortunately, I have had to prompt the supplier for information relating to the progress of my application and feed back information to them to chase up (not the other way around).  The salesman interaction was fantastic with regular feedback and contact on pricing and advice etc.  From the point of paying the deposit, contact has been with another consultant who does not seem to be chasing things up as readily as I would have liked.The contracted installers were very accomodating to our needs and installed the system in an efficient manner.Now waiting for ETSA to install import/export meter in Jan12. (Not ideal!)Point to note, the process appears to be ass about with systems being approved and installed before being able to be used, due to the installation of the Import/Export meters.  I acknowledge that this is not the fault of the retailers and installers, just a sytemic one.
The salesman Tim was very nice, honest and explained everything to us in full details and then even negotiated a price for the exact system we wanted.

The Solar system installed was well explained by sales staff and a decision was made after comparing 3 quotes, the installers arrived on time and were efficient well mannered & professional, I would have no problems in recommending Energy Aware.

So far so good, initial and follow up contacts have been very good, the two installers were very good, experienced and very reassuring.  All we need now is the ETSA component and we're off and running.

Big problem with the setup. I was promised solar panels from Canadian Solar but instead short before the scheduled installation date got a call from Energy Aware and was told that I'm getting TianWey panels instead and if I want to wait for Canadian Solar panels I would miss this year rebate deadline and my system will cost me $2000 more. Not happy. Would go with another company if I could start over again.

Energy aware was good but really just a sales team. Originally told I could have 2.81w but installer basically took charge once they arrived on site and pretty much worked out the capacity, 11 cells, 2.1w-ish changed inverter, quoted and installed new switchboard (had been told by previous electricians that if any new work was done to house this would need to be done).

I am very happy with the service I received from Energy Aware and in spite of some difficulty experienced by the installer he overcame the problem. He finished the job on Friday but was so late he could not commission the system due to lack of sun light but said he would return this coming Tuesday.  The only issue I do have is that I wanted, and was quoted for, Canadian Solar Panels but due, I was given to understand, to a supply problem, the installer arrived with and fitted Tian Wei panels.  I will take this matter up with Energy Aware as I was advised that the Canadian panels were more expensive and better quality than the Chinese panels.

From the initial enquiry re quotes to after installation of the solar panels, Tim Parkinson was fantastic.  He was very helpful and professional.  The electricians who installed the panels were excellent.
This company was the only ones who were friendly, not pushy and answered questions.

These people came to the house to inspect prior to quotation (with aerial photos).Had quoted andgiven a installation time on the same day. They then proceeded to keep me up to date by E mail.As of yesterday (25th May)the system was installed on time. I now await electrical inspectionbooked in for tomorrow (27th May).I could not be happier with the service that the have shown.

Energy Aware were knowledgable about their products and provided on request all information regarding manufacturer, model number, etc of both inverter & panels quoted.  We researched the manufacturers' then compared capability/performance of units & length of warranties with other comparable brands. If German made equals China made in all respects, then price was the only real consideration.  The German based supplier of inverter & Canada based supplier of panels both own their own manufacturing plants in China and also have offices located here in Australia for warranty claims etc and we were able to obtain information we wanted from their websites.Energy Aware have been efficient, co-operative and provided a most satisfactory service to us. Installation was within 3 weeks of signing agreement and paying deposit.  Just now waiting on our electricity supplier to changeovel the meter.However, if it was not for Finn and his fantastic website offering advice and guidance for us to follow, then we would never have reached a conclusion or been able to wade our way through the very confusing maze of finding the right unit or agent.  Our thanks to both Finn and Energy Aware - our experience has been simple and pain free.

Although it took slightly longer than promised 8 weeks instead of 6 everything else went smoothly. Rang and booked an appointment , turned up on time, did an excellent job and cleaned up after completion. We haven't had the inspector out yet as installed four days ago but it will be interesting to see how prompt they are, we already have a smart meter so hoping sooner rather than later.
Made the effort to organize a site meeting. Responded next day to my initial interest. Kept me informed during the process. Happy to answer questions along the way.

Not yet connected to the grid, that will probably take another month or so, but so far so good.  Only extra was that a new switchboard was required which was an extra expense and not really anything to do with solar.  I was advised some years ago that it would need updating.  Must compliment the trades people I have dealt with through Energy Aware and their staff, all have been pleasant and easy to deal with, even if the job did take longer than expected.
I had to wait quite a while before installation because an inverter had to be imported. However once the inverter arrived it all happened in good time.I would not hesitate to recommend Energy Aware.

The thing that sold me was the technician who came to assess my system requirements.  He was very knowledge and helpful. None of the other companies actually came out to assess my needs.The price was also most competitive, though the prices over all were very consistent.Energy Aware required a deposit of only $300.oo while the other required S1,000.00.  The deposit amount was not a big issue but I was caught out with the insulation scheme which was discontinued before installation.  I was hard work getting my deposit back, so i figured that if I paid a smaller deposit, there is less to loose if the program should be discontinued before installation.
All positive so far but we have not been connected to the grid yet. Installed 1 week ago.
Really excellent service from start to finish. Highly recommended!

So far the solar system is working good, I cannot tell what the savings are so far as I have not received my new account. But the time from installation to up and running on the grid was not as long as I expected. Very good so far.
The response from officers in this company was very quick and nice.

Good people to do business with. Kept me informed re installation date. Actually installed a better more expensive set of panels than they originally quoted because they could no supply quoted panels by the quoted delivery date. Very satisfied with the overall experience.

Energy Aware were prompt and professional, they were prepared to amend T&C's of sale / installation to suit my needs. Their follow up has been great, we plan an installation during May. The other organisations - 1 came but never gave us na quote, the other 2 never even contacted us.You site and service is excellent in helping us understand this 'new' industry.

Hard to say much about the system quality as it is brand new and I haven't had any prior experience. But it appears to be working fine and although I don't yet have a smart or multi-directional meter, I'm sure it will all happen in good time.
They were very helpful, quick to return emails, high quality panels, a few hundred  dollars cheaper than the others, and also they take on the changes required to the smart meter.

There were several instances of miscommunication where the installers would call and give an install date, then decide not to turn up that day. It took a few attempts to hold them to a date, but this can be attributed to a back log of jobs due to teh rain throughout the latter part of 2010.All in all, the service was good and the install is a neat job.
because of rain we didn't get it installed on the date they quoted but they gave us a discount on the price.
System not yet installed  -- above for what has happened so far

We feel the company was helpful with the questions we asked and negotiated on the price.we have had to wait a while for installation as the 190W panels we were quoted on were not available at the time we placed the order and unfortunately , since then the rainy weather has caused the company to get behind with their installations. We have been promised installation in the week starting 10th January so we hope that this will go ahead otherwise we are going to be upset as we paid the deposit 17th Nov.We believe we have chosen the right company but time will tell. We had seven quotes but were not impressed with many of the other companies for various reasons.
Both suppliers were very good, the one I did not choose was by far the better option - if he sold a different system.
The unit is not installed yet
